title: 473. The Road to The Great War: The Tsar Chooses War (Part 5)

sentences.en: Corfu, 8 May 1909
sentences.zh: 科孚岛，1909年5月8日

sentences.en: Dearest Nicky, as Hinsa is returning for your birthday, I gladly seize the opportunity to send you these lights.
sentences.zh: 亲爱的尼基，既然欣萨要回去参加你的生日，我很高兴抓住这个机会给你送去这些灯。

sentences.en: With all my heart, I wish you many happy returns.
sentences.zh: 我全心全意祝愿你年年有今日，岁岁有今朝。

sentences.en: May heaven bless and protect you and your wife and children.
sentences.zh: 愿上帝保佑并庇护你、你的妻子和孩子们。

sentences.en: May you be successful in your work for your country and the welfare of your people.
sentences.zh: 愿你在为国家和人民谋福祉的工作中取得成功。

sentences.en: Will you kindly accept as birthday present a watercolour sketch made by a clever croffet painter representing the Achilleon, seen from the olive grove at the foot of the hill.
sentences.zh: 请务必收下这份生日礼物，这是一位聪明的科孚画家画的水彩写生，描绘了从山脚橄榄树林望去的阿喀琉斯宫。

sentences.en: We spent a lovely time there under a blue sky, surrounded by sweet scents and flowers, sitting on the marble terraces in the shade of fine palm trees.
sentences.zh: 我们在那儿度过了一段美好的时光，蓝天之下，花香四溢，坐在大理石露台上，享受着精美棕榈树的荫凉。

sentences.en: Oh, I hope that once I may be able to show you this paradise when you chance to be yachting in the Mediterranean.
sentences.zh: 噢，我希望有朝一日，当你恰好在地中海游艇旅行时，我能带你看看这片天堂。

sentences.en: Oh, the island is lovely and the people quiet, simple and very polite.
sentences.zh: 噢，这座岛屿很可爱，人们安静、淳朴且非常有礼貌。

sentences.en: And no tourists.
sentences.zh: 而且没有游客。

sentences.en: Now, goodbye, dearest Nicky.
sentences.zh: 好了，再见，亲爱的尼基。

sentences.en: Best love to Alex and the children, especially the boy.
sentences.zh: 代我向亚历克斯和孩子们问好，特别是那个男孩。

sentences.en: God bless and protect you.
sentences.zh: 上帝保佑并庇护你。

sentences.en: Au revoir, I hope.
sentences.zh: 再见，希望如此。

sentences.en: And believe me, ever, your most affectionate and devoted friend and cousin, Vili.
sentences.zh: 请相信我，永远是你最深情、最忠诚的朋友和表弟，威利。

sentences.en: So, Dominic, that is a most charming letter, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 那么，多米尼克，这是一封非常迷人的信，不是吗？

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: Full of love of flowers, of the landscape of beautiful Corfu, generosity of spirit.
sentences.zh: 充满了对花朵、对美丽的科孚岛风景的热爱，以及慷慨的精神。

sentences.en: Watercolours.
sentences.zh: 水彩画。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: And people may be wondering, who is this?
sentences.zh: 人们可能会好奇，这是谁？

sentences.en: This charming man who has sent this delightful letter, this lover of watercolours, of the flowers of Greece.
sentences.zh: 这位写下这封令人愉快的信的迷人男士，这位水彩画和希腊花卉的爱好者。

sentences.en: And it's our old friend, the Kaiser.
sentences.zh: 他就是我们的老朋友，德皇。

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 正是。

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Who appears in a very unexpected light at times, doesn't he, in this series?
sentences.zh: 他在这个系列中，有时会以一种非常出人意料的形象出现，不是吗？

sentences.en: Well, we've already had him going around gardens.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们已经看过他逛花园了。

sentences.en: With Franz Ferdinand.
sentences.zh: 和弗朗茨·斐迪南一起。

sentences.en: So, we know that this is part of his character.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们知道这是他性格的一部分。

sentences.en: And, of course, this is a reminder that the Kaiser and the Tsar, you know, they're the heads of these two bristling war machines, but they're also cousins.
sentences.zh: 当然，这也提醒我们，德皇和沙皇，你知道，他们是这两台剑拔弩张的战争机器的首脑，但他们也是表兄弟。

sentences.en: They are.
sentences.zh: 他们确实是。

sentences.en: Going back to these messages later in this episode, they have been sending for many years.
sentences.zh: 回到本集后面提到的这些信息，他们已经通信多年了。

sentences.en: So, this one is five years before the outbreak of war.
sentences.zh: 所以，这一封是在战争爆发前五年写的。

sentences.en: These messages are kind of semi-public, semi-private.
sentences.zh: 这些信息算是半公开、半私人的。

sentences.en: All the stuff about Give My Love to Alex and the children, that's obviously a private and genuine message.
sentences.zh: 所有关于“代我向亚历克斯和孩子们问好”的内容，显然是私人且真诚的。

sentences.en: But foreign office officials would help the various emperors draft these messages and put in them sentiments about avoiding war and about settling, you know,
sentences.zh: 但外交部的官员会帮助各位皇帝起草这些信息，并在其中加入关于避免战争、解决争端等方面的感言，你知道的，

sentences.en: diplomatic disputes and so on.
sentences.zh: 外交纠纷等等。

sentences.en: And there's a couple of other interesting things in this one, which I found online.
sentences.zh: 这封信里还有其他几件有趣的事情，是我在网上发现的。

sentences.en: So, the Kaiser says in this letter, he says, when I went to Corfu, I was really looking forward to a proper holiday because I worked so hard.
sentences.zh: 德皇在信中说，当他去科孚岛时，他真的很期待一个像样的假期，因为他工作太辛苦了。

sentences.en: And then he says, but when we got there, we found out there's a revolution in Constantinople.
sentences.zh: 然后他说，但当我们到达那里时，发现君士坦丁堡发生了革命。

sentences.en: So, I had to do lots of paperwork.
sentences.zh: 所以我不得不处理大量的文书工作。

sentences.en: And he says to him, we poor rulers, it seems, are not entitled to holidays like other simple mortgals.
sentences.zh: 他对他说，我们这些可怜的统治者，似乎不像其他普通凡人那样有权享受假期。

sentences.en: The note of self-pity is so amusing.
sentences.zh: 这种自怜的语气真是太有趣了。

sentences.en: And then the other thing that appealed to me, the Kaiser is furious.
sentences.zh: 还有另一件事吸引了我，德皇非常愤怒。

sentences.en: He says, the papers, I work for peace, as do you.
sentences.zh: 他说，报纸上说，我和你一样致力于和平。

sentences.en: But the newspapers are always stirring up antagonism between our two countries.
sentences.zh: 但报纸总是煽动我们两国之间的敌意。

sentences.en: And he says, a lot of newspaper writers, a lot of commentators and columnists, just are completely ignorant.
sentences.zh: 他说，很多报纸撰稿人、评论员和专栏作家，简直是完全无知。

sentences.en: But more dangerous and at the same time more loathsome is that part of the press which writes what it is paid for.
sentences.zh: 但更危险、同时也更令人厌恶的是那部分拿钱办事的媒体。

sentences.en: They incite the hostility of one nation against another.
sentences.zh: 他们煽动一个国家对另一个国家的敌意。

sentences.en: And when at last, through their hellish devices, they have brought about the much desired collision.
sentences.zh: 当他们最终通过这些地狱般的手段引发了梦寐以求的冲突时，

sentences.en: They placidly sit down to watch the fight.
sentences.zh: 他们却平静地坐在一旁观看战斗。

sentences.en: So, Dominic, as an erstwhile columnist in the Daily Mail and a columnist in the Times, do you feel seen by the Kaiser?
sentences.zh: 那么，多米尼克，作为《每日邮报》的前专栏作家和《泰晤士报》的专栏作家，你觉得被德皇看穿了吗？

sentences.en: The sting of reproach?
sentences.zh: 这种责备的刺痛感？

sentences.en: I do.
sentences.zh: 我有。

sentences.en: Yeah, I feel judged by the Kaiser.
sentences.zh: 是啊，我觉得被德皇评判了。

sentences.en: That's not a good position to be in.
sentences.zh: 那可不是什么好位置。

sentences.en: Good.
sentences.zh: 很好。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: The thing that strikes me about this is that actually it's a reminder of how close he is to Austria.
sentences.zh: 这件事让我印象深刻的是，它实际上提醒了我们他与奥地利的关系有多么密切。

sentences.en: Because the Achilleon that he mentions, this is a tremendous palace, about 10 miles perhaps from the main city in Corfu.
sentences.zh: 因为他提到的阿喀琉斯宫，这是一座宏伟的宫殿，距离科孚岛主城大约10英里。

sentences.en: And it was the palace that Cici, the Princess Diana of the Austro-Hungarian Empire, the wife of Emperor Franz Joseph, and the mother of Prince Rudolf,
sentences.zh: 那是茜茜公主的宫殿，她是奥匈帝国的戴安娜王妃，弗朗茨·约瑟夫皇帝的妻子，鲁道夫王子的母亲，

sentences.en: who shot himself and thereby enabled Franz Ferdinand to become the heir to the throne.
sentences.zh: 鲁道夫王子自杀了，从而使弗朗茨·斐迪南成为了王位继承人。

sentences.en: So, that's where she retired and lived.
sentences.zh: 所以，那就是她隐居和生活的地方。

sentences.en: And the Kaiser absolutely loves it.
sentences.zh: 而德皇非常喜欢那里。

sentences.en: Have you been to it?
sentences.zh: 你去过吗？

sentences.en: Have you seen it?
sentences.zh: 你见过吗？

sentences.en: No, I've never been to Corfu.
sentences.zh: 不，我从没去过科孚岛。

sentences.en: In the garden.
sentences.zh: 在花园里。

sentences.en: I mean, it's a beautiful place.
sentences.zh: 我是说，那是个美丽的地方。

sentences.en: It really is gorgeous.
sentences.zh: 确实非常华丽。

sentences.en: And the Kaiser is not exaggerating about the beauty of its flowers.
sentences.zh: 德皇并没有夸大其花卉的美丽。

sentences.en: But out in the garden, there is an enormous statue of Achilles.
sentences.zh: 但在花园外，有一座巨大的阿喀琉斯雕像。

sentences.en: So, hence the name, the great Greek warrior, with a very, very skimpy kind of mini skirt.
sentences.zh: 所以，名字由此而来，这位伟大的希腊战士，穿着非常、非常短的迷你裙。

sentences.en: So, he's, you know, dressed as a hoplite.
sentences.zh: 他打扮成重装步兵的样子。

sentences.en: And, you know, you're upskirting.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，你在往上看。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It's very difficult to avoid gazing up at the buttocks.
sentences.zh: 很难避免盯着臀部看。

sentences.en: Well, that would put to bed all those questions that have floated around in Berlin newspapers about the semia side of the Kaiser's inner circle.
sentences.zh: 嗯，那将平息柏林报纸上关于德皇核心圈子同性倾向的所有传闻。

sentences.en: Yeah, that would resolve that.
sentences.zh: 是啊，那会解决那个问题。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And the inscription on that sculpture, although it's no longer there, but it's brilliant.
sentences.zh: 那座雕塑上的铭文，虽然现在已经不在了，但非常精彩。

sentences.en: It's, to the greatest Greek from the greatest German.
sentences.zh: 上面写着：致最伟大的希腊人，来自最伟大的德国人。

sentences.en: Oh.
sentences.zh: 噢。

sentences.en: So, tremendous modesty.
sentences.zh: 真是极其谦虚。

sentences.en: Great modesty from the Kaiser.
sentences.zh: 德皇真是太谦虚了。

sentences.en: And he's actually there.
sentences.zh: 而且他实际上就在那里。

sentences.en: He goes to Corfu, I think, pretty much every year.
sentences.zh: 我想他几乎每年都去科孚岛。

sentences.en: And he was there in 1914.
sentences.zh: 1914年他也在那里。

sentences.en: Really?
sentences.zh: 真的吗？

sentences.en: So, his happy place, I think.
sentences.zh: 所以，我想那是他的快乐之地。

sentences.en: So, in the past, you know, they have written to each other expressing their love of peace and promising to work together and all that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 过去，他们曾互相写信表达对和平的热爱，并承诺共同努力等等。

sentences.en: But, obviously, they've never faced a situation like this one.
sentences.zh: 但是，显然，他们从未面临过像现在这样的局面。

sentences.en: So, we ended last time with the expiry of the Austrian ultimatum on Saturday, the 25th of July, scenes of celebration in Vienna.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们上次结束时讲到了奥地利最后通牒在7月25日星期六到期，维也纳出现了庆祝的场面。

sentences.en: And, yes, of course, at this point, the Austrians have still not fired a shot.
sentences.zh: 是的，当然，此时奥地利人还没有开一枪。

sentences.en: So, the next day, Sunday, the 26th, they meet at about midday, all the Austrian high command.
sentences.zh: 所以，第二天，26日星期日，大约中午时分，所有奥地利高级指挥官聚在一起。

sentences.en: And, you know, the foreign minister, they say to General Conrad, who's been pressing for war all this time, right, are you ready?
sentences.zh: 你知道，外交部长对一直催促战争的康拉德将军说，好了，你准备好了吗？

sentences.en: And he says, I know, we're going to have to wait until 1922.
sentences.zh: 他说，我知道，我们得等到1922年。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: He says, I'm kind of ready.
sentences.zh: 他说，我算是准备好了。

sentences.en: I think we should probably start in mid-August would be ideal for me.
sentences.zh: 我想我们大概在八月中旬开始会比较理想。

sentences.en: That would suit me.
sentences.zh: 那样对我来说很合适。

sentences.en: Would that work for you?
sentences.zh: 这对你来说行得通吗？

sentences.en: And they're like, what?
sentences.zh: 他们心想，什么？

sentences.en: They thought he was going to start straight away.
sentences.zh: 他们以为他会马上开始。

sentences.en: So, actually, across Europe, there is a sense, even after the expiry of the ultimatum, we can work this out.
sentences.zh: 所以，实际上，在整个欧洲，即使在最后通牒到期后，人们也有一种感觉：我们可以解决这个问题。

sentences.en: We can get back from this.
sentences.zh: 我们可以挽回局面。

sentences.en: So, if you'd stop the clock at that point, Sunday, the 26th of July, and said to some of these policymakers, will there be a world war?
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你在那个时间点，7月26日星期日停下时钟，问问其中一些决策者，会发生世界大战吗？

sentences.en: I think a lot of them would have said there might.
sentences.zh: 我想他们很多人会说可能会。

sentences.en: But I'm hopeful, I have to be optimistic, that we can somehow sort all this out.
sentences.zh: 但我充满希望，我必须保持乐观，认为我们能以某种方式解决这一切。

sentences.en: So, for example, we talked last time about Sir Edward Gray, the British Foreign Secretary.
sentences.zh: 例如，我们上次谈到了英国外交大臣爱德华·格雷爵士。

sentences.en: He has put on the table a scheme for mediation, which is basically, you know, there'll be a sort of court, as it were, of Britain, France, Germany, and Italy.
sentences.zh: 他提出了一个调解方案，基本上就是，你知道，会有一个由英国、法国、德国和意大利组成的法庭。

sentences.en: And they will adjudicate the dispute between Austria and Serbia.
sentences.zh: 他们将裁决奥地利和塞尔维亚之间的争端。

sentences.en: Of course, what he doesn't know is that the window of opportunity for that, insofar it ever existed,
sentences.zh: 当然，他不知道的是，这个机会之窗，如果曾经存在过的话，

sentences.en: is closing very fast as the different nations are kind of hardening their position.
sentences.zh: 随着各国立场趋于强硬，正在迅速关闭。

sentences.en: And the next day, the Monday, the 27th, the Germans are pretty clear that they will never go along with this.
sentences.zh: 第二天，27日星期一，德国人非常明确地表示他们绝不会同意这一点。

sentences.en: And they say, look, we cannot support this, because we will be dragging our one ally and friend before a court.
sentences.zh: 他们说，看，我们不能支持这个，因为我们将把我们唯一的盟友和朋友拖上法庭。

sentences.en: Like, it needs to be arbitrated.
sentences.zh: 就像，这需要仲裁一样。

sentences.en: And actually, the Austrians have been very hard done by it.
sentences.zh: 实际上，奥地利人一直受到很不公正的对待。

sentences.en: The air has been shot.
sentences.zh: 王储被枪杀了。

sentences.en: They are entitled to take defensive measures.
sentences.zh: 他们有权采取防御措施。

sentences.en: And I think you get the first sense that day, which is the Monday, that Gray himself is beginning to lose patience and to realize that actually this might not be a success.
sentences.zh: 我想你在那天，也就是星期一，第一次感觉到格雷本人开始失去耐心，并意识到这可能不会成功。

sentences.en: So he actually makes it public for the first time.
sentences.zh: 所以他实际上第一次将其公之于众。

sentences.en: He goes into the commons and says, this is my plan.
sentences.zh: 他走进下议院说，这是我的计划。

sentences.en: I want to have a conference in London.
sentences.zh: 我想在伦敦召开会议。

sentences.en: I want to mediate.
sentences.zh: 我想进行调解。

sentences.en: And he says, you know, again,
sentences.zh: 他说，你知道，再次，

sentences.en: giving the lie to those critics who say old men took the world into war and they thought it would be over by Christmas and it would be a great laugh and a jamboree.
sentences.zh: 反驳了那些批评者的谎言，他们说老人们把世界带入了战争，他们以为圣诞节前就会结束，那会是一场盛大的欢笑和狂欢。

sentences.en: Gray says explicitly, if we don't get this right, if we don't sort it out, it will end in the greatest catastrophe that has ever befallen the continent of Europe.
sentences.zh: 格雷明确表示，如果我们不处理好这件事，如果我们不解决它，它将以欧洲大陆有史以来最大的灾难告终。

sentences.en: You know, in the cabinet, when they talk about it that evening in Britain, the mood is very gloomy.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在内阁中，当他们那天晚上在英国讨论这件事时，气氛非常阴郁。

sentences.en: And actually, a lot of the liberals say, a guy called John Burns, who was the president of the Board of Trade, why four great powers should fight over Serbia,
sentences.zh: 实际上，许多自由党人说，一个叫约翰·伯恩斯的人，他是贸易委员会主席，为什么四个大国要为塞尔维亚而战，

sentences.en: no fellow can understand.
sentences.zh: 没人能理解。

sentences.en: But four, not five.
sentences.zh: 是四个，不是五个。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Four, not five.
sentences.zh: 四个，不是五个。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 正是。

sentences.en: And what about Asquith?
sentences.zh: 那阿斯奎斯呢？

sentences.en: Is he still kind of chilling out, hanging out with his girlfriend?
sentences.zh: 他还在放松，和他的女朋友在一起吗？

sentences.en: Asquith is very chilled because he's, of course, thinking about his relationship with Venetia Stanley all this time.
sentences.zh: 阿斯奎斯非常放松，因为他当然一直都在想他和维尼蒂亚·斯坦利的关系。

sentences.en: We talked about that a little bit in a previous episode.
sentences.zh: 我们在上一集中简要谈过这一点。

sentences.en: He's completely besotted this summer with Venetia.
sentences.zh: 这个夏天他完全被维尼蒂亚迷住了。

sentences.en: After the cabinet meeting, he writes to her and he says, we had this cabinet meeting.
sentences.zh: 内阁会议结束后，他写信给她说，我们开了这个内阁会议。

sentences.en: I mean, it's unbelievable that he's betraying all these secrets.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他泄露了所有这些秘密，真是令人难以置信。

sentences.en: It's just not even really his girlfriend.
sentences.zh: 那甚至都不算是他的女朋友。

sentences.en: I mean, she's his daughter's friend.
sentences.zh: 我是说，她是她女儿的朋友。

sentences.en: And he says, Gray wants to have this conference.
sentences.zh: 他说，格雷想召开这个会议。

sentences.en: The Germans don't want to do it.
sentences.zh: 德国人不想这样做。

sentences.en: The only real hope is that Austria and Russia may come to a deal.
sentences.zh: 唯一的真正希望是奥地利和俄罗斯能达成协议。

sentences.en: But then he ends the letter.
sentences.zh: 但随后他结束了这封信。

sentences.en: That's a pretty quiet evening at the house.
sentences.zh: 那是一个相当安静的夜晚。

sentences.en: I'm actually going to get Violet.
sentences.zh: 我实际上要去接维奥莱特。

sentences.en: That's his daughter.

sentences.zh: 不要进入市中心。

sentences.zh: 但他还是照做了。

sentences.en: It's very clear, says Gray, from our lawyers, that that help could just be diplomatic, especially if the Belgians don't fight themselves.
sentences.zh: 格雷说，我们的律师很清楚，这种帮助可以仅仅是外交上的，特别是如果比利时人自己不反抗的话。

sentences.en: So if the Belgians just want us to kind of go to, I don't know, arbitration, sanctions.
sentences.zh: 所以如果比利时人只是想让我们去，我不知道，去仲裁、去制裁。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Send a sternly phrased telegram.
sentences.zh: 发一封措辞严厉的电报。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: To voice our enduring love of Belgium, Frite, whatever it might be.
sentences.zh: 表达我们对比利时、弗里特或其他什么东西的深厚感情。

sentences.en: We could just do that.
sentences.zh: 我们完全可以这样做。

sentences.en: We have the option.
sentences.zh: 我们有这个选择权。

sentences.en: He says it's a matter of policy rather than of legal obligation.
sentences.zh: 他说这更多是政策问题，而不是法律义务。

sentences.en: And even Churchill accepts that.
sentences.zh: 甚至丘吉尔也接受这一点。

sentences.en: Everybody accepts that.
sentences.zh: 所有人都接受这一点。

sentences.en: They literally get out the map.
sentences.zh: 他们真的把地图拿了出来。

sentences.en: And they get out the map on the table.
sentences.zh: 他们把地图摊在桌子上。

sentences.en: David Lloyd George, the chancellor, says, look here, probably the Germans are only going to go through the southern bit of Belgium.
sentences.zh: 财政大臣大卫·劳合·乔治说，你看，德国人可能只会穿过比利时的南部地区。

sentences.en: And in that case, everybody says, man, that case is a bit much to go to war about that, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，大家都说，伙计，为了这点事去打仗有点小题大做了吧？

sentences.en: And actually, even Churchill.
sentences.zh: 事实上，连丘吉尔也这么认为。

sentences.en: So Churchill has been going around like a firework about to go off, isn't he, this week.
sentences.zh: 所以丘吉尔这周就像个快要点燃的烟花一样到处乱窜，不是吗？

sentences.en: He keeps going around saying, I've never been happier.
sentences.zh: 他一直说，我从未如此快乐过。

sentences.en: War is coming.
sentences.zh: 战争要来了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Well, he has this brilliant letter that he writes to Clemmie, his wife, where he says, everything tends towards catastrophe and collapse.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他写给妻子克莱米的那封精彩的信里说，一切都趋向于灾难和崩溃。

sentences.en: I am interested, geared up and happy.
sentences.zh: 我感到兴奋、准备就绪，而且很快乐。

sentences.en: But even Churchill, you see, he's gagging for war because he just loves wars, says, I don't see why we should come in if they go only a little way into Belgium.
sentences.zh: 但即使是丘吉尔，你看，他因为热爱战争而渴望开战，他也说，我不明白如果他们只是稍微进入比利时一点点，我们为什么要介入。

sentences.en: And the reason they're saying that is Churchill also says war would be a calamity for the civilized nations.
sentences.zh: 他们之所以这么说，是因为丘吉尔也认为战争对文明国家来说将是一场灾难。

sentences.en: So they know, they absolutely know that great war will be a nightmare and they're keen to avoid it.
sentences.zh: 所以他们知道，他们绝对知道那场大战将是一场噩梦，他们非常希望能避免它。

sentences.en: And they are hoping that they can get out of doing it.
sentences.zh: 他们希望能置身事外。

sentences.en: So the cabinet meeting breaks up.
sentences.zh: 于是内阁会议散会了。

sentences.en: There's no decision being made.
sentences.zh: 没有做出任何决定。

sentences.en: Gray goes off and he meets a group of liberal backbenchers and they say, could you go public?
sentences.zh: 格雷离开后去见了一群自由党后座议员，他们问，你能公开表态吗？

sentences.en: Because you say Britain will stay out because that might discourage the French and the Russians.
sentences.zh: 因为如果你说英国会置身事外，那可能会让法国人和俄国人退缩。

sentences.en: And he says, no, I can't do that.
sentences.zh: 他说，不，我不能那样做。

sentences.en: I must be ambiguous.
sentences.zh: 我必须保持模糊。

sentences.en: I need a free hand.
sentences.zh: 我需要自由裁量权。

sentences.en: I don't want to be tied down because that might encourage the Germans.
sentences.zh: 我不想被束缚，因为那可能会鼓励德国人。

sentences.en: But I think you could say as a criticism of Gray that by this point, you know, he's running out of time with his ambiguity.
sentences.zh: 但我认为你可以批评格雷，因为到了这个时候，他的模糊策略已经快要耗尽时间了。

sentences.en: And actually, of course, all the time he has promised the French.
sentences.zh: 而且事实上，他一直以来都向法国人做出了承诺。

sentences.en: He has subcontracted his decision making to the French because he has promised them when it does come to the crunch, we will be there.
sentences.zh: 他把决策权外包给了法国人，因为他向他们承诺过，当关键时刻到来时，我们一定会到场。

sentences.en: And I think as much as you admire Gray, Tom, I think he is being a little bit disingenuous with his own colleagues.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，尽管你很钦佩格雷，但我认为他在对待自己的同事时有点虚伪。

sentences.en: So this is the criticism in Neil Ferguson's book, The Pity of War, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这就是尼尔·弗格森在《战争的怜悯》一书中的批评，对吧？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean,
sentences.zh: 我是说，

sentences.en: this is the case he makes against Gray and says that Gray's ambiguity encouraged the other powers to go to war and then left Britain powerless to avoid being drawn into the kind of the meat grinder itself and should have stayed out.
sentences.zh: 这就是他针对格雷提出的观点，他说格雷的模糊态度鼓励了其他大国走向战争，然后让英国无力避免被卷入那场绞肉机，本应置身事外。

sentences.en: I think you can make the case that Gray's ambiguity, I mean, obviously it doesn't work because Britain is drawn into the war and the war happens.
sentences.zh: 我认为你可以说格雷的模糊策略显然是失败的，因为英国被卷入了战争，战争还是爆发了。

sentences.en: But you can understand why he's ambiguous.
sentences.zh: 但你可以理解他为什么保持模糊。

sentences.en: And the other thing I think about the criticism of Gray, actually, having made that criticism about the ambiguity,
sentences.zh: 关于对格雷的批评，我还有一点想法，实际上，在提出了关于模糊性的批评之后，

sentences.en: I think people have a tendency to assume that rather like now when something happens, everyone blames the Americans, even if the Americans don't really control it at all.
sentences.zh: 我认为人们有一种倾向，就像现在发生什么事时，每个人都责怪美国人，即使美国人根本无法控制它一样。

sentences.en: They say, well, the Americans should have stopped it.
sentences.zh: 他们会说，嗯，美国人本该阻止它的。

sentences.en: The American Secretary of State was asleep.
sentences.zh: 美国国务卿当时在睡觉。

sentences.en: The American Secretary of State should have sorted all this out.
sentences.zh: 美国国务卿本该解决这一切的。

sentences.en: But sometimes it's just not the big powers.
sentences.zh: 但有时这并非大国所能左右。

sentences.en: It's not in their power.
sentences.zh: 这不在他们的权力范围内。

sentences.en: You know, Gray did all that he could.
sentences.zh: 你知道，格雷已经尽了他所能做的一切。

sentences.en: Well, I think also because he has access to all the telegrams and papers and he's the one who's focusing on it, even more than anyone else in cabinet.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为这也是因为他能接触到所有的电报和文件，他是比内阁中任何人都更关注此事的人。

sentences.en: Is thinking it cannot be possible that we go to war over this.
sentences.zh: 他在想，我们为了这个去打仗是不可能的。

sentences.en: Our interests are not directly tied to it.
sentences.zh: 我们的利益并没有直接与此挂钩。

sentences.en: It just seems unbelievable.
sentences.zh: 这简直令人难以置信。

sentences.en: But the truth of the fact that they're kind of trapped in this system is dawning on him faster than it is on his other colleagues.
sentences.zh: 但他们被困在这个体系中的事实，正比他的其他同事更快地在他脑海中浮现。

sentences.en: Oh, definitely.
sentences.zh: 哦，绝对是。

sentences.en: I think definitely by this point, the 28th, 29th, I think definitely by this point, at the back of his mind,
sentences.zh: 我想到了28号、29号，到了这个阶段，他心里肯定有一种感觉，

sentences.en: I think there's a cold feeling that you get when you know there's no escaping the disaster, but you just don't want to admit it to everybody else.
sentences.zh: 我想当你意识到灾难无法避免时，会有一种冰冷的感觉，但你只是不想向其他人承认这一点。

sentences.en: But actually, as I've said, I don't think London is the great cockpit of this story.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，正如我所说，我不认为伦敦是这个故事的核心战场。

sentences.en: I mean, we're telling it from a British perspective because we're British, but also because Britain is at this point the world's greatest power.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我们从英国的角度来讲述它，因为我们是英国人，也因为英国在此时是世界上最强大的国家。

sentences.en: So it makes a huge difference whether Britain's in the war or not.
sentences.zh: 所以英国是否参战有着巨大的影响。

sentences.en: But the people who are driving it are Vienna, Belgrade, Berlin and St. Petersburg.
sentences.zh: 但真正推动局势的是维也纳、贝尔格莱德、柏林和圣彼得堡。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But also we're looking at Britain because Britain hasn't yet made up its mind, whereas all the other participants have.
sentences.zh: 但我们关注英国也是因为英国还没有下定决心，而其他所有参与者都已经决定了。

sentences.en: Or have they?
sentences.zh: 或者说他们真的决定了吗？

sentences.en: Because that morning, our old friend, the Kaiser, wakes up in Potsdam.
sentences.zh: 因为那天早上，我们的老朋友，德皇，在波茨坦醒来。

sentences.en: And of course, he still thinks there's not going to be a war, hopes there's not going to be a war.
sentences.zh: 当然，他仍然认为不会有战争，希望不会有战争。

sentences.en: And he is delighted to wake to a telegram.
sentences.zh: 他很高兴醒来时收到了一封电报。

sentences.en: See, this is the reason we began with Corfu, with that letter.
sentences.zh: 看，这就是我们从科孚岛那封信开始的原因。

sentences.en: He wakes to one of these messages from Nicky, his cousin, the Tsar.
sentences.zh: 他醒来时收到了来自他的表弟，沙皇尼基发来的信息之一。

sentences.en: And the Tsar says, you know, this is a very serious moment.
sentences.zh: 沙皇说，你知道，这是一个非常严肃的时刻。

sentences.en: I need your help.
sentences.zh: 我需要你的帮助。

sentences.en: None of us want a war.
sentences.zh: 我们谁都不想打仗。

sentences.en: I beg you in the name of our old friendship to do what you can to stop your allies from going too far.
sentences.zh: 我以我们旧日友谊的名义恳求你，尽你所能阻止你的盟友走得太远。

sentences.en: By which he means Austria-Hungary.
sentences.zh: 他指的是奥匈帝国。

sentences.en: Now, this telegram was Nicholas's own personal idea.
sentences.zh: 现在，这封电报是尼古拉个人的主意。

sentences.en: Nicholas is in some ways a very irritating man.
sentences.zh: 尼古拉在某些方面是一个非常令人恼火的人。

sentences.en: He's very autocratic.
sentences.zh: 他非常专制。

sentences.en: He's very stubborn.
sentences.zh: 他非常固执。

sentences.en: He's too reactionary, all of that stuff.
sentences.zh: 他太反动了，诸如此类。

sentences.en: But he hates the thought of war.
sentences.zh: 但他讨厌战争的想法。

sentences.en: He abhors it.
sentences.zh: 他厌恶战争。

sentences.en: And he is desperate to stop it.
sentences.zh: 他拼命想阻止它。

sentences.en: And he's surrounded by ministers who are egging him on to sign mobilization orders.
sentences.zh: 而他周围的部长们都在怂恿他签署动员令。

sentences.en: And he says, I want to send my cousin a telegram that will sort this out.
sentences.zh: 他说，我想给我的表弟发一封电报，这能解决问题。

sentences.en: Now, as it happens, it overlaps with one that Willi has sent him.
sentences.zh: 碰巧的是，这与威利发给他的电报重叠了。

sentences.en: And Willi has sent him a telegram that says, I'm trying to restrain the Austrians, which I have to say, he sort of is.
sentences.zh: 威利发给他的电报说，我正在努力克制奥地利人，我必须说，他确实在某种程度上做到了。

sentences.en: But the other people in Berlin are not.
sentences.zh: 但柏林的其他官员却并非如此。

sentences.en: And he says, come on, Nicky, you and I hate terrorists and regicides.
sentences.zh: 他说，来吧，尼基，你我都讨厌恐怖分子和弑君者。

sentences.en: These people should get their deserved punishment, Wilhelm says in this telegram.
sentences.zh: 这些人应该得到他们应得的惩罚，威廉在这封电报中说。

sentences.en: I understand how difficult it is for you and your government to face the drift of your public opinion.
sentences.zh: 我理解你和你的政府在面对舆论导向时有多么困难。

sentences.en: But please help me to resolve this.
sentences.zh: 但请帮我解决这个问题。

sentences.en: So they've both got these telegraMs.
sentences.zh: 所以他们都收到了这些电报。

sentences.en: And then Willi writes another one.
sentences.zh: 然后威利又写了另一封。

sentences.en: And he says, listen, I think the Austrians are behaving in self-defense.
sentences.zh: 他说，听着，我认为奥地利人的行为是出于自卫。

sentences.en: I promise you they won't seize any Serbian territory.
sentences.zh: 我向你保证，他们不会占领任何塞尔维亚领土。

sentences.en: They won't annex it after the war is over.
sentences.zh: 战争结束后他们不会吞并它。

sentences.en: Please don't mobilize your armies because I'm hoping to mediate between you and the Austrians.
sentences.zh: 请不要动员你的军队，因为我希望能在你和奥地利人之间进行调解。

sentences.en: And that would make it impossible for me to do so.
sentences.zh: 那样做会让我无法调解。

sentences.en: So Wilhelm sends this.
sentences.zh: 于是威廉发出了这封电报。

sentences.en: Now, Nicholas, he's not the sharpest tool in the cutlery drawer, the Tsar.
sentences.zh: 现在，尼古拉，沙皇并不是最聪明的人。

sentences.en: He gets this telegram that evening.
sentences.zh: 那天晚上他收到了这封电报。

sentences.en: And he says, oh, my God, this is brilliant.
sentences.zh: 他说，天哪，这太棒了。

sentences.en: Cousin Willi has come through after all.
sentences.zh: 表弟威利终究还是帮了忙。

sentences.en: And he rings.
sentences.zh: 他打电话。

sentences.en: You know how much he hates using the phone.
sentences.zh: 你知道他有多讨厌用电话。

sentences.en: He rings the foreign minister and he says, great news.
sentences.zh: 他打电话给外交大臣说，好消息。

sentences.en: The Kaiser hates the thought of war.
sentences.zh: 德皇讨厌战争的想法。

sentences.en: So do I.
sentences.zh: 我也一样。

sentences.en: I've actually been thinking and I have changed my mind.
sentences.zh: 我其实一直在思考，我已经改变主意了。

sentences.en: I don't like the thought of going to war at all.
sentences.zh: 我一点也不想打仗。

sentences.en: When Sazanov, the foreign minister, hears this, he is gutted.
sentences.zh: 当外交大臣萨佐诺夫听到这个消息时，他感到非常沮丧。

sentences.en: Because actually all day, he and the other ministers have been deciding what to do.
sentences.zh: 因为事实上整整一天，他和部长们都在决定该怎么做。

sentences.en: And they have decided they will go for a general mobilization.
sentences.zh: 他们已经决定进行总动员。

sentences.en: Now, I think this is sometimes underrated, especially in popular histories that take a very kind of anti-German line.
sentences.zh: 现在，我认为这一点有时被低估了，特别是在那些采取非常反德立场的通俗历史中。

sentences.en: Because this is a massive step in the escalation of the crisis.
sentences.zh: 因为这是危机升级过程中的一个重大步骤。

sentences.en: Because nobody yet has had a general mobilization, not even the Austrians.
sentences.zh: 因为目前还没有人进行总动员，连奥地利人也没有。

sentences.en: No, definitely not the Germans.
sentences.zh: 不，绝对不是德国人。

sentences.en: No, the Germans are nowhere near it.
sentences.zh: 不，德国人离那还远着呢。

sentences.en: So for the Russians to have done this.
sentences.zh: 所以俄国人竟然这么做了。

sentences.en: Now, look, I understand why they did it.
sentences.zh: 你看，我理解他们为什么这么做。

sentences.en: They think they've got to steal a march on everybody else because they happen to be so big and lumbering and slow.
sentences.zh: 他们认为自己必须抢在所有人前面行动，因为他们实在太庞大、太笨重、太迟缓了。

sentences.en: But for them to do this, as Thomas Otte says in his book, July Crisis, which is actually very critical of Germany and Austria.
sentences.zh: 但正如托马斯·奥特在他的著作《七月危机》中所说，他们竟然这么做——这本书其实对德国和奥地利持非常批判的态度。

sentences.en: But he says of Russia at this point.
sentences.zh: 但他此时是这样评价俄国的。

sentences.en: They rushed into this decision.
sentences.zh: 他们仓促地做出了这个决定。

sentences.en: The Austrians were still maybe 10 days off from a full attack on Serbia.
sentences.zh: 奥地利人距离全面进攻塞尔维亚可能还有10天的时间。

sentences.en: So there was still time.
sentences.zh: 所以时间还来得及。

sentences.en: They didn't need to force the pace of events in this way.
sentences.zh: 他们本不需要以这种方式强行推进事态发展。

sentences.en: And that once the Russians had gone down that road, it's really hard to see how you get out of this without a war.
sentences.zh: 而且一旦俄国人走上了那条路，真的很难看出如何才能在不爆发战争的情况下脱身。

sentences.en: Because that's terrifying for the Germans.
sentences.zh: 因为这对德国人来说太可怕了。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: To have this massive great leviathan on your doorstep mobilizing.
sentences.zh: 家门口竟然有这样一个庞然大物在进行动员。

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: Imagine a similar situation now.
sentences.zh: 想象一下现在类似的情况。

sentences.en: Imagine if suddenly you heard that Russian troops are massing on the borders of Poland or something.
sentences.zh: 想象一下，如果你突然听说俄军正在波兰边境集结之类的消息。

sentences.en: I mean, you don't think, oh, they'll probably just all go home afterwards.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你不会觉得，哦，他们事后大概都会回家吧。

sentences.en: You think, oh, my God, this is war.
sentences.zh: 你会想，天哪，这是要打仗了。

sentences.en: We have to immediately act.
sentences.zh: 我们必须立即采取行动。

sentences.en: Otherwise, they'll just walk straight in.
sentences.zh: 否则，他们就会直接打进来了。

sentences.en: That's what the Germans think.
sentences.zh: 这就是德国人的想法。

sentences.en: Now, the thing is, the Tsar knows this, Nicholas.
sentences.zh: 现在的问题是，沙皇尼古拉知道这一点。

sentences.en: And when he hears this, he says, no.
sentences.zh: 当他听到这个消息时，他说，不。

sentences.en: These are his words.
sentences.zh: 这是他的原话。

sentences.en: I will not be responsible for a monstrous slaughter.
sentences.zh: 我绝不会对一场可怕的屠杀负责。

sentences.en: And quite rightly, he says to his ministers, war would be disastrous for the world.
sentences.zh: 他非常正确地对大臣们说，战争对世界来说将是一场灾难。

sentences.en: Once it had broken out, it would be difficult to stop.
sentences.zh: 一旦爆发，就很难停止了。

sentences.en: The German emperor had frequently assured him of his sincere desire to safeguard the peace of Europe.
sentences.zh: 德国皇帝曾多次向他保证，自己真诚地希望维护欧洲和平。

sentences.en: And it had always been possible to come to an agreement with the Kaiser, even in serious cases.
sentences.zh: 而且即使在严重的情况下，也总是能够与德皇达成协议。

sentences.en: And you know what?
sentences.zh: 你知道吗？

sentences.en: If those monarchs had had as much power as people often think they did, then there would have been no world war.
